structures.title: be going to
structures.content: a. affirmative: I'm going to buy a magazine with my pocket money. b. negative: We aren't going to go on holiday this year. c. questions: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

structures.title: Time expression + will, when + will
structures.content: I'll see you tomorrow / next week / this summer / soon. When I go on holiday, I'll buy some souvenirs.

structures.title: would like
structures.content: would like + infinitive: a. affirmative: I'd like to visit Canada. b. negative: Jess wouldn't like to babysit. c. questions: Would you like to go shopping? d. short answers: Yes, I would. / No, I wouldn't.

structures.title: Present perfect
structures.content: a. affirmative: I've seen lots of monuments. He / She / [It]'s visited interesting places. You / We / They've lived in many different countries. b. negative: I haven't read the new novel. He / She / [It] hasn't been on a yacht. You / We / They haven't flown by helicopter. Questions: Have I / you / we / they been in the USA? Has he / she / [it] seen the TV programme? Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. Yes, he has. / No, he hasn't.

structures.title: Present perfect + for and since
structures.content: I've been a supporter for two years. I've been a supporter since 2002. I've been a supporter since I was 13.

structures.title: Tense review
structures.content: present simple, present continuous, past simple, past continuous, present perfect, will, be going to

structures.title: should / shouldn't
structures.content: a. affirmative: You should go to the doctor if you feel ill. b. negative: You shouldn't forget to eat fruit and vegetables. c. questions: Should you tell an adult? d. short answers: Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.

structures.title: must / mustn't
structures.content: a. affirmative: He must go to the hospital if his condition gets serious. b. negative: You mustn't react to a bully's behaviour. c. questions: Must I tell my teacher? d. short answers: Yes, you must. / No, you mustn't.

grammar_non_textbook: Review of present simple and present continuous
Growing range of quantifiers: all, both, any, a few, a lot (of), a lot, (too) much, (too) many
Review of past simple and past continuous
Modal verbs to talk about rules and obligation in past and present: must, mustn't, have to, don't have to, had to, didn't have to
Question tags to show interest / request clarification
Infinitive of purpose: She went to the shops to buy a new bag for school.
